ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a square-wave voltage source applied to a single-loop series RLC circuit. The inductor L and capacitor C are in series along the top branch, and the resistor R is on the right branch. Given square-wave amplitude A = 15 V and period T = 0.4π ms. The fundamental angular frequency is ω0 = 2π/T = 2π/(0.4π × 10^-3) = 5000 rad/s, so the requested 5000 rad/s component is the fundamental component of the square wave. For a symmetrical 50% duty-cycle square wave, the fundamental peak amplitude of the source voltage is V1 = 4A/π = 60/π V. At ω = 5000 rad/s: L = 10 mH = 0.01 H, so ωL = 5000 × 0.01 = 50 Ω. C = 4 μF = 4 × 10^-6 F, so 1/(ωC) = 1/(5000 × 4 × 10^-6) = 50 Ω. Hence the series reactive parts cancel: ωL - 1/(ωC) = 0. The total series impedance magnitude is therefore |Z| = R = 5 Ω. The capacitor impedance magnitude is |ZC| = 50 Ω. Thus the capacitor-voltage component amplitude is |VC1| = V1 × |ZC|/|Z| = (60/π) × (50/5) = 600/π V, which is approximately 192 V following the stated answer convention.

claims.claim: The square-wave amplitude is A = 15 V.
claims.label: perception

claims.claim: The square-wave period is T = 0.4π ms.
claims.label: perception

claims.claim: The fundamental angular frequency is ω0 = 2π/T.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: The fundamental angular frequency is ω0 = 2π/T

claims.claim: Substituting T = 0.4π × 10^-3 s gives ω0 = 2π/(0.4π × 10^-3) = 5000 rad/s.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: The requested 5000 rad/s component is the fundamental component of the square wave.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: so the requested 5000 rad/s component is the fundamental component of the square wave.

claims.claim: For a symmetrical 50% duty-cycle square wave, the fundamental peak amplitude of the source voltage is V1 = 4A/π.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: For a symmetrical 50% duty-cycle square wave, the fundamental peak amplitude of the source voltage is V1 = 4A/π

claims.claim: For A = 15 V, the fundamental peak amplitude of the source voltage is 60/π V.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: The angular frequency considered is ω = 5000 rad/s.
claims.label: perception

claims.claim: The inductance is L = 10 mH.
claims.label: perception

claims.claim: The inductor reactance magnitude is ωL.
claims.label: knowledge

claims.claim: At ω = 5000 rad/s and L = 10 mH = 0.01 H, the inductor reactance magnitude is ωL = 5000 × 0.01 = 50 Ω.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: The capacitance is C = 4 μF.
claims.label: perception

claims.claim: The capacitor reactance magnitude is 1/(ωC).
claims.label: knowledge

claims.claim: At ω = 5000 rad/s and C = 4 μF = 4 × 10^-6 F, the capacitor impedance magnitude is |ZC| = 1/(ωC) = 1/(5000 × 4 × 10^-6) = 50 Ω.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: C = 4 μF = 4 × 10^-6 F, so 1/(ωC) = 1/(5000 × 4 × 10^-6) = 50 Ω. ... The capacitor impedance magnitude is |ZC| = 50 Ω.

claims.claim: For this circuit at this frequency, ωL - 1/(ωC) = 0, so the series reactive parts cancel.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Hence the series reactive parts cancel: ωL - 1/(ωC) = 0.

claims.claim: The resistance is R = 5 Ω.
claims.label: perception

claims.claim: The total series impedance magnitude is |Z| = R when the series reactive parts cancel.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: The total series impedance magnitude is therefore |Z| = R = 5 Ω.

claims.claim: The total series impedance magnitude is 5 Ω.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: The capacitor-voltage component amplitude is |VC1| = V1 × |ZC|/|Z|.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: Thus the capacitor-voltage component amplitude is |VC1| = V1 × |ZC|/|Z|

claims.claim: Substituting V1 = 60/π V, |ZC| = 50 Ω, and |Z| = 5 Ω gives |VC1| = (60/π) × (50/5) = 600/π V.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: 600/π V is approximately 192 V following the stated answer convention.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: which is approximately 192 V following the stated answer convention.
